passages.text: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
passages.sermon: A man named Lazarus was sick.\r\nLazarus lived in Bethany.\r\nBethany was the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
passages.original: Ἦν δέ τις ἀσθενῶν Λάζαρος ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς

passages.text: (Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)
passages.sermon:
Mary lived in Bethany.
Mary had a sister named Martha.
Mary had a brother named Lazarus.
Lazarus was sick.
Mary was the woman who would anoint the Lord Jesus with perfume.
Mary would wipe Jesus’ feet with her hair.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ Μαριὰμ ἡ ἀλείψασα τὸν Κύριον μύρῳ καὶ ἐκμάξασα τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἧς ὁ ἀδελφὸς Λάζαρος ἠσθένει

passages.text: So the sisters sent word to Jesus, “Lord, the one You love is sick.”
passages.sermon:
Mary and Martha were sisters.
Their brother was Lazarus.
Lazarus was sick.
Jesus loved Lazarus.
Mary and Martha sent a message to Jesus.
They said, “Lord, the one you love is sick.”
passages.original: ἀπέστειλαν οὖν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσαι Κύριε ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ

passages.text: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard the message about Lazarus.
Jesus spoke about the sickness.
Jesus said, “This sickness will not end in death.
This sickness is for the glory of God.
God will receive glory through this sickness.
The Son of God will be glorified because of it.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Αὕτη ἡ ἀσθένεια οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ἀλλ’ ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ δι’ αὐτῆς

passages.text: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus loved Martha.
Jesus loved Martha’s sister.
Jesus loved Lazarus.
Jesus cared deeply for all three.
passages.original: Ἠγάπα δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον

passages.text: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days, and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard that Lazarus was sick.
Jesus stayed in the place where He was.
He stayed there for two days.
After two days, Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "Let us go back to Judea."
passages.original: ὡς οὖν ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἀσθενεῖ τότε μὲν ἔμεινεν ἐν ᾧ ἦν τόπῳ δύο ἡμέρας ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς Ἄγωμεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν

passages.text: “Rabbi,” they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They called Him “Rabbi.”
They said, “The Jews just tried to stone You.”
They asked, “Are You going back there again?”
passages.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί Ῥαββί νῦν ἐζήτουν σε λιθάσαι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ πάλιν ὑπάγεις ἐκεῖ

passages.text: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “There are twelve hours in the day.
If a person walks during the day, he does not stumble.
He does not stumble because he sees the light of this world.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὐχὶ δώδεκα ὧραί εἰσιν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐάν τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ οὐ προσκόπτει ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει

passages.text: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”
passages.sermon: If a person walks at night, he will stumble.\r\nHe stumbles because he does not have light in him.
passages.original: ἐὰν δέ τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ νυκτί προσκόπτει ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Lazarus is our friend.
Lazarus has fallen asleep.
I am going to him.
I will wake him up.”
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἶπεν καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει αὐτοῖς Λάζαρος ὁ φίλος ἡμῶν κεκοίμηται ἀλλὰ πορεύομαι ἵνα ἐξυπνίσω αὐτόν

passages.text: His disciples replied, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them that Lazarus had fallen asleep.
The disciples answered Jesus.
They said, “Lord, if Lazarus is sleeping, he will recover.”
passages.original: Εἶπαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτῷ Κύριε εἰ κεκοίμηται σωθήσεται

passages.text: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the death of Lazarus.
The disciples thought Jesus meant natural sleep.
Jesus did not mean natural sleep.
Jesus meant that Lazarus had died.
passages.original: εἰρήκει δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἔδοξαν ὅτι περὶ τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου λέγει

passages.text: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead, and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He spoke very clearly.
Jesus said, “Lazarus is dead.”
Jesus said, “I am glad for your sake that I was not there.”
Jesus wanted His disciples to believe in Him.
Jesus said, “Let us go to Lazarus.”
passages.original: Τότε οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς παρρησίᾳ Λάζαρος ἀπέθανεν καὶ χαίρω δι’ ὑμᾶς ἵνα πιστεύσητε ὅτι οὐκ ἤμην ἐκεῖ ἀλλὰ ἄγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.”
passages.sermon:
Thomas was one of Jesus’ disciples.
People also called Thomas “Didymus.”
Thomas spoke to the other disciples.
He said, “Let us go too.”
He said, “We will die with Jesus.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος τοῖς συμμαθηταῖς Ἄγωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἀποθάνωμεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.
passages.sermon: Jesus arrived in Bethany.\r\nHe found Lazarus.\r\nLazarus had been in the tomb for four days.
passages.original: Ἐλθὼν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὗρεν αὐτὸν τέσσαρας ἤδη ἡμέρας ἔχοντα ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ

passages.text: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, a little less than two miles away, and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.
passages.sermon:
Bethany was a village.
Bethany was close to Jerusalem.
Bethany was about two miles from Jerusalem.
Many Jews came to Bethany.
These Jews came to visit Martha and Mary.
They came to comfort Martha and Mary.
Martha and Mary had lost their brother.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ ἡ Βηθανία ἐγγὺς τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίων δεκαπέντε πολλοὶ δὲ ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐληλύθεισαν πρὸς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ Μαριὰμ ἵνα παραμυθήσωνται αὐτὰς περὶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ

passages.text: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him; but Mary stayed at home.
passages.sermon: Martha heard that Jesus was coming.\r\nMartha went out to meet Jesus.\r\nMary stayed at home.
passages.original: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ Μαριὰμ δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο

passages.text: Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
passages.sermon: Martha spoke to Jesus.\r\nShe said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν ἡ Μάρθα πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν Κύριε εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου

passages.text: But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.”
passages.sermon:
Martha spoke to Jesus.
Martha believed in Jesus.
Martha said she still trusted God.
Martha said, “Even now, I know this.”
Martha said, “God will give You whatever You ask.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν Θεὸν δώσει σοι ὁ Θεός

passages.text: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Martha.\r\nJesus said, “Your brother will rise again.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀναστήσεται ὁ ἀδελφός σου

passages.text: Martha replied, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
passages.sermon:
Martha spoke to Jesus.
Martha said she knew something about her brother.
Martha said, "I know he will rise again."
Martha said this would happen at the resurrection.
Martha said the resurrection will happen on the last day.
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Martha.
Jesus said, “I am the resurrection.
I am the life.
Anyone who believes in Me will live.
He will live even if he dies.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται

passages.text: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Martha.\r\nJesus said, “Everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die.\r\nDo you believe this?”
passages.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα πιστεύεις τοῦτο

passages.text: “Yes, Lord,” she answered, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.”
passages.sermon:
Martha spoke to Jesus.
She said, “Yes, Lord.”
Martha said she believed in Jesus.
She said, “I believe you are the Christ.”
She said, “You are the Son of God.”
She said, “You are the one who was to come into the world.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί Κύριε ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος

passages.text: After Martha had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her, “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”
passages.sermon:
Martha spoke to Jesus.
She then left.
Martha called her sister Mary.
She spoke to Mary quietly.
Martha said, “The Teacher is here.”
Martha also said, “He is asking for you.”
passages.original: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα Ὁ Διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε

passages.text: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.
passages.sermon:
Mary was the sister of Martha.
Mary heard that Jesus was calling for her.
Mary got up quickly.
Mary went to Jesus.
passages.original: ἐκείνη δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν ἠγέρθη ταχὺ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus had not entered the village yet.\r\nHe was still at the place where Martha met Him.
passages.original: Οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην ἀλλ’ ἦν ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα

passages.text: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.
passages.sermon:
Some Jews were in the house with Mary.
These Jews were consoling Mary.
They saw Mary get up quickly.
They saw Mary go out of the house.
They followed Mary.
They thought Mary was going to the tomb.
They thought Mary was going there to mourn.
passages.original: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν ἰδόντες τὴν Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ

passages.text: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
passages.sermon:
Mary was the sister of Lazarus.
Mary came to the place where Jesus was.
Mary saw Jesus.
Mary fell at Jesus’ feet.
Mary spoke to Jesus.
Mary said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
passages.original: ἡ οὖν Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς πόδας λέγουσα αὐτῷ Κύριε εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἄν μου ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός

passages.text: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw Mary weeping.
The Jews who came with Mary were also weeping.
Jesus felt deeply moved in His spirit.
Jesus became troubled.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν

passages.text: “Where have you put him?” He asked. “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people with Mary.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Where have you put him?”
The people answered Jesus.
They said, “Lord, come and see.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κύριε ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε

passages.text: Jesus wept.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus saw the people weeping.
Jesus felt deep sorrow.
Jesus wept.
passages.original: Ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”
passages.sermon: The Jews saw Jesus weep.\r\nThey spoke about Jesus.\r\nThey said, “See how He loved him!”
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν

passages.text: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?”
passages.sermon:
Some people stood there.
They saw Jesus.
Jesus had opened the eyes of a blind man.
These people spoke to each other.
They asked a question about Jesus.
They said, “Could not this man have kept Lazarus from dying?”
They wondered if Jesus could have stopped Lazarus from dying.
passages.original: Τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ

passages.text: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.
passages.sermon:
Jesus felt deep emotion again.
Jesus came to the tomb.
The tomb was a cave.
A stone lay across the entrance of the cave.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπ’ αὐτῷ

passages.text: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said. “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke.
He said, “Take away the stone.”
Martha answered Him.
Martha was the sister of the man who had died.
She said, “Lord, by now he stinks.”
She said, “It has already been four days.”
passages.original: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα Κύριε ἤδη ὄζει τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Martha.
Martha was the sister of the dead man.
Jesus said, “Did I not tell you this?”
“If you believe, you will see the glory of God.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.
passages.sermon:
The people took away the stone.
Jesus was present at the tomb.
Jesus lifted His eyes upward.
Jesus spoke to God the Father.
Jesus said, “Father, I thank You.”
Jesus thanked God because God had heard Him.
passages.original: Ἦραν οὖν τὸν λίθον ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἄνω καὶ εἶπεν Πάτερ εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι ἤκουσάς μου

passages.text: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to God the Father.
Jesus said, “Father, I know that You always hear Me.”
Jesus said this aloud for the people standing nearby.
Jesus wanted the people to believe that God the Father sent Him.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ᾔδειν ὅτι πάντοτέ μου ἀκούεις ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον τὸν περιεστῶτα εἶπον ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας

passages.text: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood at the tomb.
He had just spoken to God the Father.
Jesus then called out loudly.
He said, “Lazarus, come out!”
passages.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐκραύγασεν Λάζαρε δεῦρο ἔξω

passages.text: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had just called Lazarus out of the tomb.
Lazarus had been dead.
Lazarus came out of the tomb.
His hands were bound with strips of linen.
His feet were also bound with strips of linen.
A cloth wrapped his face.
Jesus spoke to the people standing there.
Jesus said, “Unwrap him.”
Jesus said, “Let him go.”
passages.original: ἐξῆλθεν ὁ τεθνηκὼς δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας κειρίαις καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ σουδαρίῳ περιεδέδετο Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε αὐτὸν ὑπάγειν

passages.text: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.
passages.sermon: Many Jews came to Mary.\r\nThese Jews saw what Jesus did.\r\nThese Jews believed in Jesus.
passages.original: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ἃ ἐποίησεν ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
passages.sermon:
Some people saw what Jesus did.
These people were among the Jews who had come to Mary.
Some of them left the others.
They went to the Pharisees.
They told the Pharisees what Jesus had done.
passages.original: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was the Jewish ruling council.
The chief priests and Pharisees spoke to the council.
They said, “What should we do?”
They said, “This man is doing many signs.”
They referred to Jesus.
Jesus was performing many miraculous signs.
passages.original: Συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον καὶ ἔλεγον Τί ποιοῦμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ποιεῖ σημεῖα

passages.text: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the Pharisees spoke about Jesus.
They said, “If we let Jesus continue like this, everyone will believe in Him.
Then the Romans will come.
The Romans will take away our place.
The Romans will take away our nation.”
passages.original: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος

passages.text: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all!
passages.sermon:
Caiaphas was one of them.
Caiaphas was the high priest that year.
Caiaphas spoke to them.
Caiaphas said, “You know nothing at all!”
passages.original: Εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν

passages.text: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”
passages.sermon:
Caiaphas was the high priest that year.
Caiaphas spoke to the council.
He said, “You do not understand something important.
It is better for you if one man dies for the people.
This is better than the whole nation being destroyed.”
passages.original: οὐδὲ λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται

passages.text: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation, and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.
passages.sermon:
Caiaphas was the high priest that year.
He did not speak these words by himself.
He was prophesying.
He said that Jesus would die for the nation.
Jesus would not die only for the nation.
Jesus would also die for the scattered children of God.
Jesus would gather the scattered children of God into one.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνήσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν

passages.text: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.
passages.sermon: The Jewish leaders decided to kill Jesus.\r\nThey made this decision on that day.\r\nThey began to plan how to kill Him.
passages.original: Ἀπ’ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The Jewish leaders plotted to kill Jesus.
Because of this, Jesus stopped walking openly among the Jews.
Jesus left that place.
He went to a region near the wilderness.
He went to a town called Ephraim.
Jesus stayed in Ephraim.
His disciples stayed with Him.
passages.original: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν κἀκεῖ ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν

passages.text: Now the Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.
passages.sermon:
The Jewish Passover was near.
Many people lived in the countryside.
These people went up to Jerusalem.
They went before the Passover.
They wanted to purify themselves.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς

passages.text: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”
passages.sermon:
Many people stood in the temple courts.
They looked for Jesus.
They talked to each other.
They asked, “What do you think?”
They said, “Will Jesus come to the feast?”
passages.original: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετ’ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν

passages.text: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the Pharisees were Jewish religious leaders.
They gave strict orders to the people.
They told everyone to report if anyone knew where Jesus was.
They wanted this information so they could arrest Jesus.
passages.original: δεδώκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν
